description: Our vision is to lead the world toward a modern future rooted in science and discovery, by illuminating the path through the profound darkness of space—much like pulsars.
summary:
**ASTRA Care** is an offline-capable astronaut health intelligence desktop platform designed for spaceflight crews. We developed an interactive dashboard featuring a clickable, color-coded human body map, dynamic longitudinal and cross-domain charts, a mission data-completeness checklist with readiness XP and badges, cognitive (PVT-B/DSST) and ocular (IOP/SANS) assessments, and eight specialist AI models—covering oxygen saturation (Chronos), blood pressure and glucose (TabPFN-v2), musculoskeletal bone and lean mass, sleep and fatigue, immune/sepsis markers, radiation and EVA dosimetry, wearable stress (MOMENT), and ECG-FM—paired with a local MedGemma and NASA/clinical RAG assistant.

It addresses the challenge by letting astronauts enter vitals manually, import telemetry files, or complete interactive check-ins; comparing readings against personal baselines; adapting guidance across mission environments (Space Station, Spacecraft, Pressurized Rover, Lunar Base, and Mars Base); and providing beginner-friendly measurement instructions, color-coded risk alerts, and flight-surgeon escalation thresholds.

This is important because deep-space missions face communication delays and limited medical support, requiring crews to detect multi-system health shifts early, take preventive action, and triage risks autonomously.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ASTRA Care is an offline-first desktop health intelligence platform for astronauts. Crew members can import CSV/JSON telemetry, enter manual vitals and blood sugar readings, run an interactive PVT-B / DSST cognitive check-in, or log Eye Pressure (IOP) exams—all persisted locally in SQLite databases (measurements.db, analysis.db, astra_desktop.db).

The frontend communicates with a local orchestration layer (launch_services.py / desktop.py) that routes data to 8 specialist AI/ML microservices (:8010–:8016) and a local RAG + LLM server (astra_rag on :8000):

  • SpO₂ / Chronos: Forecasts oxygen saturation quantiles (q10/q50/q90) from time-series telemetry.
  • Cardiometabolic (BP & Glucose / TabPFN-v2 + LightGBM): Compares systolic/diastolic BP, MAP, pulse pressure, shock index, resting HR, fasting glucose, and HbA1c against personal baselines and ACC/AHA 2017 & ADA rules.
  • MSK & Bone: Evaluates bone mineral density (BMD), appendicular lean mass, Vitamin D, and calcium intake.
  • Sleep & Fatigue / Cognitive: Tracks sleep debt, HRV (RMSSD), nocturnal movement, and a multi-index convergence trigger for PVT-B/DSST testing.
  • Immune & Laboratory: Screens WBC, neutrophils, lymphocytes, platelets, albumin/globulin, CRP, and SIRS/sepsis indicators.
  • Radiation & EVA: Combines dosimeter readings, habitat shielding, and cached/live NOAA GOES proton flux data.
  • Wearable / MOMENT & ECG-FM: Classifies multi-channel wearable stress anomalies and interprets 12-lead ECG-FM scores.
  • MedGemma + NASA RAG: Generates grounded explanations, citations, and environment-aware next-step actions.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Early multi-system risk detection: Cross-domain longitudinal charts and color-coded status badges (Nominal, Elevated, Warning, Critical) reveal subtle correlations (e.g., sleep debt + cognitive slowing + musculoskeletal decline) before emergencies develop.
  • Accessible to non-physician crew: Built-in beginner-friendly "How to measure & why it matters" guides explain microgravity measurement techniques and clear Flight Surgeon escalation thresholds.
  • Mission readiness & engagement: A crew-wide data-completeness checklist, active routine prompts, readiness XP, ranks, and achievement badges keep daily and weekly monitoring consistent.
  • Intended Impact: Empower astronauts on long-duration orbital, lunar, and Mars missions—where Earth communication can be delayed by up to ~22 minutes—to monitor health autonomously, take preventive countermeasures early, and triage risks safely.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware Used

  • Languages: Python 3.12, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, C# (.NET launcher), SQL (SQLite), PowerShell.
  • AI/ML & Data Stack: PyTorch (torch 2.11.0+cu128), TabPFN-v2, LightGBM, Chronos, MOMENT, ECG-FM, scikit-learn (Random Forest for IOP), MedGemma (medgemma1.5:4b-it-q4_K_M via Ollama), and a custom NumPy/JSON/NPY vector RAG engine (astra_rag).
  • UI & Visualization: Three.js orbital navigator, custom interactive SVG human body map, SVG multi-series charts, and Edge/Chromium app-mode desktop hosting (serve_browser.py).
  • Hardware: Local workstation with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (CUDA-accelerated TabPFN-v2 & PyTorch inference) alongside CPU-compatible fallbacks.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

  • Creativity: Combines a futuristic obsidian/nebula aerospace UI with an interactive anatomical body hologram color-coded from live crew telemetry, a Mission Environment Context switcher (Space Station, Spacecraft, Pressurized Rover, Lunar Base, Mars Base) that adapts MedGemma guidance and default radiation shielding without altering raw clinical measurements, and gamified mission-readiness tracking.
    1. Personal baselines over generic averages: Every crew profile stores individual resting baselines (HR, BP, SpO₂, Temp, Sleep) so deviations are judged against the astronaut's own norm.
    2. Strict data integrity: Missing values are never fabricated or silently filled; irregular series and out-of-range inputs are explicitly flagged.
    3. Offline resilience & safety: Full core functionality works without internet, all protocols cite verified NASA/WHO/ADA/ACC-AHA sources, and outputs are framed as decision support requiring specialist review rather than automated diagnosis.
